newsitem.title: USA: US Airways to assess Shuttle's value.
newsitem.headline: US Airways to assess Shuttle's value.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc said it started to assess the value of the US Airways Shuttle but had made no decision on whether to buy the commuter service.
In a federal filing released Monday, US Airways said it recently "exercised its right to commence a procedure to value Shuttle Inc, the owner of the US Airways Shuttle."
The Shuttle, which provides flights from New York to Boston and Washington, is owned by creditors of its former owner, Donald Trump. It is operated by USAir.
US Airways said the "initiation of the valuation procedure" did not represent a commitment to purchase the Shuttle.
Its exclusive right to buy the Shuttle operations ends April 9, but the company has the right to match any purchase offer made by another party over the next five years.
"Any decision to purchase the Shuttle, either through the valuation procedure or the right of first refusal, will made based on price and related business considerations," the company said.

Analysts expect US Airways to delay its decision on the Shuttle until it reaches a new labor pact with its pilots and finalizes plans to set up a low-cost unit to compete with rivals such as Southwest Airlines Co and Delta Air Lines Inc's Express unit.

"They can match any offer for five years. There is no rush. The bigger priority at USAir is starting informational road show with employees," said Julius Maldutis, an airline analyst with Salomon Brothers.
